MAHALAGANG ABISO SA MGA MOTORISTA 🚦

Asahan ang mabigat na daloy ng trapiko sa mga sumusunod na kalsada sa September 7, 10, at 14, 2025, mula 2:00AM - 7:00AM at 2:00PM - 7:00PM, upang bigyang-daan ang isasagawang 2025 Bar Examinations na gaganapin sa New Era University (NEU) sa kahabaan ng Central Avenue, Quezon City:

• Commonwealth Ave. papasok ng Central Ave.
• Visayas Ave. papasok ng Central Ave.

Samantala, mananatili namang bukas ang iba pang kalsada para sa regular na daloy ng trapiko, ngunit mahigpit na ipapatupad ang NO PARKING sa kahabaan ng Central Avenue.

Mahigpit ding ipinagbabawal ang SALUBONG, PANINIGARILYO, at MAGUGULO/MAIINGAY NA AKTIBIDAD sa kahabaan ng Central Avenue.

Magtutulungan at nakaantabay ang mga tauhan ng Traffic and Transport Management Department (TTMD) at Department of Public Order and Safety (DPOS) para maisaayos ang daloy ng trapiko sa nasabing lugar.

Pinapayuhan ang mga motorista na dumaan sa mga alternatibong ruta.

Maraming salamat po sa inyong pang-unawa.

LOOK: Protesters from various militant groups gather outside the Senate of the Philippines on Wednesday, September 10, to condemn alleged anomalies in flood control projects.

Carrying placards and chanting slogans, they call on lawmakers to hold those involved accountable and to put an end to corruption in government-funded infrastructure programs.

The groups say their demonstration aims to pressure the Senate to take stronger action, even in the absence of a formal inquiry on the issue at the time of their protest.

📷: Mark Balmores | MB

data.text:
DPWH'S CASINO ROYALE: LACSON LINKS 'BGC BOYS' TO MONEY LAUNDERING

Senate President Pro Tempore Ping Lacson on Tuesday accused five former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) officials—dubbed the "BGC Boys"—of gambling away taxpayers' money in casinos and possibly laundering funds intended for flood control projects.

In a privilege speech, Lacson said the group—known to casino employees as the Bulacan Group of Contractors—used aliases and fake driver's licenses to conceal their identities while incurring nearly ₱950 million in gross gambling losses across 13 casinos in Metro Manila, Cebu, and Pampanga.

The five were identified as Henry Alcantara, sacked DPWH Region 4A assistant regional director, alias Joseph Castro Villegas; Brice Ericson Hernandez, Bulacan OIC district engineer, alias Marvin Santos de Guzman; Jaypee Mendoza, assistant district engineer, alias Peejay Asuncion; Arjay Domasig, DPWH engineer II, alias Sandro Bernardo Park; and Edrick San Diego.

Lacson cited casino records showing Hernandez lost ₱435 million and Mendoza ₱418 million, while Alcantara, Domasig, and San Diego recorded millions more in losses. Yet the same records also reflected suspicious multimillion-peso winnings, which Lacson said may have been used to legitimize illicit funds.

"Sinuwerte nga kayang sabay sabay na nanalo ang mga ito, Mr. President? O baka naman money laundering scheme?" Lacson said.

He added that their gambling violated Presidential Decree 1869, RA 6713, and other laws prohibiting public officials from entering casinos, while their use of fake IDs and aliases constituted separate criminal offenses.

Because of this, Lacson said he has referred the names and aliases of the five to the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) and sought the freezing of their bank accounts.

"Sumatutal, habang lubog pa rin sa tubig-baha ang mga taga-Bulacan dahil sa mga pangungurakot ng mga ito, at kahit buking na mismo ng Pangulo ang kalokohan, sige pa rin ang pagpapasasa ng BGC Boys — sa pagwawaldas ng pera ng taumbayan. Walang kahiya-hiya sa katawan. Wala pong konsensya ang mga ito, Mr. President," he said.

Beyond accountability, Lacson called for reforms, including a perpetual ban on blacklisted contractors with ghost or substandard projects, heavier penalties for conflicts of interest under the Contractors' License Law and RA 6713, and stricter transparency in the planning and funding of infrastructure projects, including requiring detailed engineering designs before the release of funds.

"Mr. President, these people have reduced the lives of our flood stricken countrymen into living hell. It is time to give them what they rightly deserve," Lacson concluded.
